problem: MedicalRecordsDetailPage combines record composition with attachment loading, partial-source reconciliation, scan-status presentation, signed-download validation, and route-stale completion handling.
desired_outcome: Move the attachment panel and its local loading/open workflow to a medical-record feature slice while leaving route lifecycle, navigation context, and page composition in MedicalRecordsDetailPage.
user_journey: Open a medical record and review record-linked and encounter-linked attachments.
Distinguish a confirmed empty list from loading, full failure, and partial-source failure.
Open an attachment only when scanning marks it available and the API returns a matching, unexpired signed content URL.
If the route changes during a read or URL request, ignore the stale completion and reset feature state for the new record.

current_evidence.claim: The page owned attachment list state, two-source merge, status/error text, download URL validation, window opening, and route generation checks.
Existing MedicalRecordsDetailPage tests cover loading/empty, metadata rendering, signed URL confirmation, invalid target URL, and source failure.
The application is a Vue 3 Vite SPA and this route already composes domain components with local feature composables.

unknowns.question: Does the extracted card retain visual parity in a real browser across narrow layouts and dark theme?
unknowns.falsification: Compare rendered screenshots at desktop and narrow widths in light and dark themes.

unknowns.question: Do real assistive technologies announce the status, errors, and available actions as expected?
unknowns.falsification: Run the browser journey with keyboard-only input and a screen reader.

constraints: The API remains the source of truth for attachment metadata, scanning status, authorization, and signed URLs.
Preserve the existing record-linked and encounter-linked queries, identity filters, deduplication, newest-first ordering, and partial-failure wording.
Retain the page generation guard and reset attachment state when the record route changes.
Do not open a content URL until its attachment path, token, origin, and expiry are validated.
Keep the existing diagnostics navigation context and add no package or route dependency.

render_environment.server: API owns attachment records, scan state, authorization, and signed URL issuance
render_environment.client: The page owns route validity and the feature owns the attachment panel and transient open/read workflow
render_environment.hydration: No SSR hydration boundary is used for this route

browser_targets: Current evergreen browsers supported by the app
ux_invariants: Loading never appears as a confirmed empty state.
A full or partial read failure is visible and does not claim the missing source has no attachments.
Only available attachments expose an open action.
An unconfirmed, mismatched, external, or expired content URL is never opened.
accessibility_invariants: The panel remains a labelled list of attachments.
Loading and scan availability retain status semantics; read and action failures retain alert semantics.
Open buttons retain a file-specific accessible name and busy state.
At narrow widths, metadata and actions reflow without horizontal overflow.
data_invariants: Attachment data remains server-owned and is not cached or persisted in the browser.
Only entries linked to the current medical record or encounter are projected.
Duplicate attachment IDs are represented once and entries remain newest first.
A route-stale response cannot replace the active record's attachment state.

state_classification.scope: Medical record and encounter attachment metadata
state_classification.derivation: Feature filters, deduplicates, and orders exact linked records
state_classification.sync_requirement: Read fresh metadata for each record route; request a signed URL only when the user opens a file

state_classification.source_of_truth: Current list operation and open action
state_classification.derivation: User action and current route request
state_classification.sync_requirement: Reset on record route change; reject stale completions

state_classification.source_of_truth: Attachment scan state and validated URL response
state_classification.scope: One attachment row and open attempt
state_classification.derivation: Available status controls action; matching unexpired URL controls navigation
state_classification.sync_requirement: Recompute for each response and current route guard

state_ownership.state: Attachment list, loading, read error, open error, and opening ID
state_ownership.reset: Reset when the page starts a new record route load

state_ownership.state: Current record ID and page generation
writers: Vue Router route change and page load
state_ownership.reset: Increment on route load and invalidate on unmount

writers: Controlled feature props and open event

data_ownership.client_projection: Feature accepts only rows linked to the current medical record or encounter and merges duplicate IDs
data_ownership.mutation_owner: No attachment metadata mutation is performed; open requests a signed download URL
data_ownership.staleness: Page route generation plus feature sequence guard rejects stale reads and opens

client_owned: Matching signed URL validation before opening
server_client_boundary.serialization: No SSR serialization or hydration boundary is used

trust_boundary.server_enforcement: API remains responsible for authorization, tenant scoping, attachment ownership, scanning, and token validity
trust_boundary.residual_risk: Client checks prevent opening an unexpected URL; they do not replace server authorization

candidates.name: Keep attachment markup and workflow in the page
candidates.cost: Maintains attachment list, URL trust checks, and route race handling inside the already large medical-record page

candidates.name: Global attachment store
candidates.fit: Could share attachment state across unrelated routes
candidates.cost: No demonstrated cross-route cache or synchronization need; adds shared ownership and invalidation risk

candidates.name: Feature panel plus local composable
candidates.fit: Groups attachment presentation and its route-scoped loading/open workflow
candidates.cost: Adds two internal modules and controlled props without adding a package or request

simple_baseline: Keep route identity in the page and render a controlled panel; feature state remains local to the medical-record route.

rejected_candidates.reason: Attachments are only consumed by this route here, and no shared cache or cross-route sync contract exists.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Move route generation and patient/record loading into the attachment feature
rejected_candidates.reason: The page already owns cross-domain route lifecycle; moving it would couple an attachment feature to patient, encounter, billing, and clinical record state.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Open the returned URL directly without validation
rejected_candidates.reason: A mismatched or expired response could navigate away from the application or open a different attachment.

selected_pattern: Route-scoped feature composable with a controlled attachment panel.
selection_rationale: The attachment list, failures, scan eligibility, and signed-open flow form one domain journey and can be tested independently. The page keeps the route-generation source of truth and supplies a guard; the feature owns only its ephemeral state. The choice is based on observed state and responsibility concentration, not line count alone.

typed_driver_evidence.evidence: The route currently handles two attachment sources, linkage filtering, partial failure, scan-status gating, signed URL validation, and open feedback.
Existing tests already verify loading, empty, partial failure, open URL confirmation, and bad target behavior at the page boundary.

component_boundaries.name: useClinicalRecordAttachments
component_boundaries.accessibility_contract: Supplies loading, error, opening, and scan state for the panel

component_boundaries.name: ClinicalAttachmentsPanel
component_boundaries.accessibility_contract: Preserves labelled list, status/alert semantics, file-specific action names, and busy state

component_boundaries.name: MedicalRecordsDetailPage
component_boundaries.accessibility_contract: Preserves the surrounding medical-record landmarks and focus flow

illegal_states: claiming empty while loading or failed
opening mismatched or expired content URL
stale route completion changing current feature state
state_contract.owner: Composable owns attachment state; page owns route identity and invalidation

data_fetching_contract.query_identity: Current medical record ID plus encounter ID
data_fetching_contract.deduplication: Merge by attachment ID after filtering exact link type and ID
data_fetching_contract.cancellation: Existing requests are not aborted; page route guard and feature generation ignore stale results
data_fetching_contract.stale_policy: Load once during current record context resolution; stale completion is discarded
data_fetching_contract.error_policy: Preserve confirmed rows on partial failure and distinguish an unknown list from confirmed empty

mutation_semantics.idempotency: No persistent attachment mutation; download URL request retains existing API semantics
mutation_semantics.pending: One opening ID disables other open actions during URL preparation
mutation_semantics.duplicate_guard: Composable rejects another open while one request is pending
mutation_semantics.rollback: Failed URL validation or blocked browser window leaves the record page intact and shows an action error
mutation_semantics.invalidation: Record route reset clears all attachment feature state

loading_behavior: Show a polite busy status while both sources settle; do not show the empty message until a confirmed result exists.
empty_behavior: Show the existing confirmed-empty message only when there is no attachment read error.
error_behavior: Show full or partial list errors separately from open-action errors; retain confirmed rows on a partial result.
recovery_behavior: Record route reload retries the reads; an open error leaves the user on the record so they can retry.
responsive_behavior: Preserve card styling and stack attachment metadata/actions at the existing 820px breakpoint.
keyboard_focus_behavior: Use the existing design-system button and file-specific accessible action name; no new focus trap or modal is introduced.
assistive_behavior: Preserve list/listitem roles, polite loading and scan statuses, alert roles for failures, and button busy state.
motion_behavior: No new motion or transition is introduced.

performance_budget.workload: One medical record with record-linked and encounter-linked attachment metadata
performance_budget.baseline: Existing two list-source requests and one user-triggered signed URL request
performance_budget.target: No additional request or dependency; retain existing list and open request sequence
performance_budget.hard_max: Do not add requests to the attachment journey
performance_budget.measurement: Compare the request call sequence in tests; browser bundle measurement is not required because the feature stays in the current route chunk

bundle_impact: Adds two modules to the existing route chunk and no package dependency or route-level split.
rendering_impact: No route rendering mode change; the controlled panel updates from local feature refs.
network_impact: Preserves the two-source read and one signed URL request on user action.
security_implications: Attachment links and metadata remain text interpolation; no HTML rendering is added.
The API remains responsible for attachment authorization, tenant scope, scan enforcement, and signed-token validity.
The client opens only a same-origin relative URL with the exact attachment content path, token, and future expiry.

testing_requirements.claim: Filtering/merge, partial errors, route staleness, signed URL target/expiry checks, and pending reset remain correct.
Loading, confirmed empty, errors, metadata, scan eligibility, accessible names, and open event remain correct.
Route context, loading call, and stale route integration remain correct.

runtime_evidence_required: Open a confirmed attachment from the medical-record page
accessibility_evidence_required: Real browser screen-reader status and error announcement check
performance_evidence_required: No additional request relative to the existing page sequence

migration.strategy: Extract the current attachment markup and behavior in place without changing API DTOs or route ownership.
migration.compatibility_window: No API compatibility window required; the medical-record URL and attachment service calls remain stable.
migration.rollback: Restore inline panel and attachment state from the parent if focused tests reveal a regression.

rollout: Internal Vue composition refactor behind the existing medical-record route with no feature flag.

unresolved_risks.risk: Component and composable tests cannot establish real browser visual parity or assistive-technology announcements.
unresolved_risks.mitigation: Preserve the existing DOM roles and text states; keep screenshot and assisted review open as separate evidence.
unresolved_risks.revalidation: Before claiming full browser or accessibility acceptance for M-22/M-25.

unresolved_risks.risk: Client validation does not authorize access and cannot replace API tenant, scan, or signed-token enforcement.
unresolved_risks.mitigation: Keep server/API negative tenant tests and target-backed authorization evidence as M-27/M-28 gates.
unresolved_risks.revalidation: Before production acceptance of attachment access.

handoff.trigger: M-22 requires rendered visual and assistive evidence
Attachment authorization and tenant isolation are server-owned

revalidation_trigger: Revisit when attachment listing, scan status, signed URL shape, record route lifecycle, or API trust contract changes.
